archetypes.name: dual-impl-parity
archetypes.rationale: This plan modifies both a live Bash path and a Python migration path; structural drift between the two is a primary failure mode the plan itself names.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that every gate, flag, exit code, and edge-case branch introduced in `scripts/ship-pr.sh` has a structurally equivalent counterpart in `python/ci_monitor.py`. Check that the `_fix_dispatched_on_ready_log` (Bash) and `fix_dispatched_on_ready_log` (Python) tracking variables are set under the same conditions and gate the same terminal outcome (`ci-fix-exhausted` vs `fix-exhausted`/`Outcome.NEEDS_USER_INPUT`). Verify that `logs.state == 'ready'` (Python) and `gh_logs_rc == 0` (Bash) are truly equivalent in every code path the plan claims they are, including error and in-progress branches. Confirm that the in-progress-only exhaustion path explicitly remains exit 4 / `STALLED` in both implementations, not only in one. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: test-plan-gaps
archetypes.rationale: The plan rewrites existing test cases and adds new ones across three test files; a mis-specified or incomplete test plan can leave acceptance criteria untested.
archetypes.prompt_body: Cross-check each acceptance criterion from the issue against the named test additions and rewrites in the plan: verify that at least one test case in `python/test_ci_monitor.py` or `scripts/test-ship-pr-fix-loop-2632.inc.sh` covers each of the four acceptance bullets (deterministic triggers fix, transient-vs-deterministic distinction, no pure retry on test/lint/compile, both implementations updated). Verify that the plan to rewrite `vendor_loop_ci_fix_exhausted` and `ci_fix_exhausted` in `scripts/test-ship-pr.sh` correctly shifts assertions from exit 4 stall to exit 3 `ci-fix-exhausted` without silently dropping the guard that in-progress / no-ready-log exhaustion still exits 4. Check whether the tail-window edge case (network signature buried above the 100-line tail) and the rebase-storm exit-4 case each have a corresponding test or are explicitly acknowledged as untested. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: bail-reason-consumers
archetypes.rationale: The plan introduces a new bail-reason token `ci-fix-exhausted` and routes it to exit 3; any consumer of exit 3 or `BAIL_REASON` not updated in the plan becomes a silent breakage.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every consumer of `BAIL_REASON`, `is_autonomous_exit3_bail_reason`, `needs_user_bail_reason`, and exit-3 handling in `scripts/ship-pr.sh` and `skills/implement/SKILL.md` to confirm the plan lists all sites that need updating for `ci-fix-exhausted`. Verify that the plan to extend `needs_user_bail_reason` and `is_autonomous_exit3_bail_reason` (~line 1720/1728) is complete — that no other branch or case statement in `ship-pr.sh` dispatches on these functions but is absent from the plan's change list. Check that the SKILL.md Step 8+ extension to fire on `ci-fix-exhausted` (not only `first-fixer-non-health`) cannot accidentally double-trigger the autonomous sub-procedure if both bail reasons appear in a single run. Verify the `ci-decide.md` documentation update correctly distinguishes `ci-fix-exhausted` (autonomous, exit 3) from `fix-attempts-exhausted` in `ci-decide.sh` (operator, exit 3, `BAIL_NEEDS_USER_INPUT=true`) so operators reading the doc cannot conflate the two paths. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
